analysis: The PR changes only one documentation line, docs/architecture/inference.md line 1163 (base and head), in the supported model_type table. For gpt_oss, it adds a note that bf16 checkpoints keep bf16 activations and native K/V on every layer, because the expert SwiGLU clamp's scalar bounds take the activation dtype (it cites libs/mlx-swift-lm/Libraries/MLXLLM/Models/GPTOSS+Experts.swift, swiglu). The existing statements remain unchanged: historical complete checkpoints are default-on for exact gpt-oss-20b, and native contiguous/paged paths require observed dtype/capability gates. Relevant threat entries are T-041 (SSD prefix-cache bindings, including observed dtypes and layoutEpoch), T-027/T-012 (weights) and TB-007. The text documents numeric precision behavior and does not change cache identity, salt scoping, the TTL, the kill switch, encryption or authorization. The line keeps the observed-dtype gate statement. The rest of the surrounding text in units 4–6 (lines 808–1586) is unchanged base text and was examined only for context. The referenced Swift source was not supplied, so this pass cannot confirm whether the code itself changed. If an accompanying code change alters K/V dtypes, an integration pass should check that SSD checkpoint dtype bindings (CBv2PagedKVWriteValidation, observed native types) still fail closed. No security regression or threat-model gap was identified in the documentation change.
